summary: Picks one of a few views or modes, shown side by side as attached buttons: the brand of a preview, the density, light or dark. The choice applies at once, on the current screen.
whenToUse: Switching how the same content is shown: Light or Dark, Comfortable or Compact, Grid or List.

Short options where seeing every option at once helps the choice: two to five usually, more for filters people switch between often (status filters). On a phone the track scrolls sideways and never widens the page.
Appearance strong when the control is what the view is about (the status filter of a list): the selected segment fills with Deep Harbor. At most one strong control per view.
The change applies immediately, with no Save button.
Size sm in toolbars, menus and dense panels; md everywhere else. Heights follow the density setting.
fullWidth inside a narrow panel or menu, so the segments share the width equally.
whenNotToUse: Switching between panels of different content: use Tabs, which link each tab to its panel.
A setting in a form that is saved later: use RadioGroup, which shows a label and help per option.
Long labels, or options people pick once and forget: use Select.
Turning one thing on or off: use Switch.
Triggering actions (Export, Delete): use Button or an attached ButtonGroup.

dos.title: Short, parallel labels
dos.text: One or two words per segment, same grammatical form, so the set reads as one choice.

dos.title: Label outside the track
dos.text: Put a visible label to the left of the track, as a caption on its center line, and name the group with it (aria-labelledby, or the same words in label). The track holds the options and nothing else.

dos.title: Strong for the control the view is about
dos.text: A list filtered by status: the selected filter fills with Deep Harbor, the strongest signal on the screen. Six short filters are fine; on a phone they scroll sideways.

dos.title: Always start with a selection
dos.text: A segmented control shows the current mode. Pass value or defaultValue so one segment is always selected.

donts.title: Actions dressed as segments
donts.text: Segments select a mode; they never run a command. "Export" and "Share" belong on buttons.

donts.title: The label inside the track
donts.text: Never put the group's label in the same pill as the options. Inside one container it reads as one more option ("Brand" next to "Bridge" and "Ocean"). Keep it outside, to the left.

donts.title: Too many or too long options
donts.text: Two or three words per segment make the track longer than the screen and stop reading as one control. Keep labels to one or two words, or use Select.

accessibility: Base UI RadioGroup with native button radios: role radiogroup on the row, role radio and aria-checked on each segment.
Tab enters the group on the selected segment and leaves it; arrow keys move the selection, Home and End jump to the ends.
Give the group a name: aria-labelledby pointing at the visible label outside the track, or label (aria-label) when the context already names it.
The selected segment is marked by a raised plate (or the Deep Harbor fill with strong) and a darker text color, not by color alone.
When the track scrolls, arrow keys still move the selection and the selected segment scrolls into view.
The focus ring (focus.ring.color) shows on keyboard focus only.
Rendered without JavaScript, the HTML keeps role, aria-checked and data-value, so a small script can drive it: flip aria-checked and tabindex, and handle arrow keys.
contentGuidelines: Sentence case nouns or adjectives: "Compact", "Dark", "Grid". No verbs: segments are states, not actions.
One or two words. Drop the shared word: "Light, Dark", not "Light theme, Dark theme".
Name the group with what is being chosen: "Density", "Brand", "Themes shown". When it changes only a preview, say so: "Preview brand".
A visible label is a caption to the left of the track (caption size, muted text color), never a segment inside it.

anatomy.strong: Strong appearance: Deep Harbor selected segment
anatomy.leading: Decoration before the label, for example a color swatch
anatomy.label: Label
